data.body: Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23 (queue review). restamp_api.py (and so every wave:N tag stamped before 2026-10-23) counted a phase used as a prerequisite as 1 + the depth of the phase's OWN needs, ignoring its open tasks: a task behind a whole-phase hold such as P-docs-generic was stamped wave 1 when it cannot start until that phase's 9-deep chain is done (wave 10); 890 of 1581 tags were wrong, 6 to 28 waves too low, and doc and research kinds were not stamped at all. D-wave-semantics already says 'wave N = 1 + the highest wave among open prerequisites': make core.schedule depth (GR-wave-derived) implement that for phases: wave(phase) = max(wave of its open tasks, 1 + wave of its own needs); a task inherits its phase's needs; doc/research/job kinds count. Regression test: a task whose phase needs another phase with a 3-deep chain gets wave 4, not 1; a stale hand tag is reported by doctor. Reference implementation: docs/ddflow/research/scripts/wave_stamp_accurate.py (added by the queue review).
data.title: Wave derivation counts a phase prerequisite as the wave of its last open task, and covers doc and research kinds

data.body: Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23. DX-queue-lint covers overlaps, duplicates, missing globs and stale references. A review of 1581 open tasks also needed, by hand: (1) needs edge from a fix-/DX- task to a feature task (RH rule: never; 6 found, 1 removed: fix-B-mcp-required-falsy -> MTD-next-hints); (2) a task that needs a whole phase (146 edges; 5 EXT-* tasks narrowed to one building block) -- report when its text names a task of that phase; (3) decide/research/probe/bug tasks whose only blocker is an inherited phase hold (ACF-decide, PI-decide, SPEC-decide were); (4) a producer whose text lists 'CONSUMERS (add needs)' or 'Entry tasks to wait for it' where a listed consumer has no path to the producer (HX-facts-core, SE-globs-agent-phases, B-tpl-readme-regions, B-sched-backpressure: 19 edges were missing); (5) a needs edge that makes a tiny task wait for a deep chain it does not use (SE-globs-agent-phases waiting for SE-globs would have delayed 67 tasks by 4 waves): report the depth each edge adds. Each class is a [plan_lint] rule with a knob and a --fix proposal, never an automatic edit. Regression tests: one fixture per class that fails on a lint without it.
data.title: plan lint reports the edge classes a queue review found by hand: fix/DX needing a feature, whole-phase needs naming one task, held decide/research/bug tasks, producer-listed consumers without an edge

data.body: Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23. 42 open phases still listed B-gap-log-scale/lanes/plan-lint, P-unify and others as needs long after they were done, so 'waits for six ids' read as a live hold; 596 tasks carry 1047 more. They gate nothing but make show, brief and every graph reader noisier, and a script must filter them. Decide with the operator: (a) ddflow cleanup/doctor offers to remove them in one batch (one event per item, ~600 events: weigh against log growth), or (b) the fold keeps them in the log but exposes needs_open and needs_done separately and show/brief print only the open ones. Distinct from RH-prune-needs, which removes TRANSITIVELY redundant edges (602 found, all among live items; the 2026-10-23 review left them: removing one whose intermediate edge is later dropped silently loses the dependency). Regression test: a phase needing a done item shows it only under 'satisfied'.
data.title: Satisfied needs edges are pruned or hidden: 1047 task edges and 116 phase edges pointed at done items

data.body: Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23: the width and critical-path figures of the queue review (per phase: tasks, ready now, longest intra-phase chain, widest level; per wave: tasks and independent lanes when tasks sharing a literal file are joined; the critical path as a list of ids) were computed by a throwaway script (docs/ddflow/research/scripts/queue_width.py). DX-waves-status gives counts per wave and state; this adds the parallelism view: how many agents can usefully work at once, which file serialises a wave (README.md joined 71 tasks and 2131 unordered pairs; ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py 63; ddflow/config.py 54), and what the critical path is, with a --what-if 'without these needs' for a hold the operator is considering (lifting the docs-wave hold: critical path 37 -> 30, total depth -33%). Read-only.
data.title: ddflow plan width: ready-set width, intra-phase chain length and critical path per phase and wave, lanes by glob component

data.body: Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23: 9185 pairs of open tasks share a literal file with no order between them (README.md 2131, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py 1683, ddflow/config.py 1137, core/model.py 392, services/review.py 374, implement-phase.md 348). The lease serialises them at run time, so the cost is waiting for files (fx-cilock waited 1285 s) and the second task rebasing a design it did not see. The cure is not more needs edges (a 71-task README chain would serialise the docs of the whole product) but fewer tasks naming the file: docs-only tasks use fragments (P-change-surface.docs-fragments), knobs go in per-feature config sections, MCP in action groups. Add a plan-check warning when a task adds a hot file from a configurable list to its globs while a fragment or registry route exists, show the count in plan check, and migrate the open tasks whose only README edit is a docs section. Regression test: a task adding README.md to its globs after the fragments engine exists is warned.
data.title: A budget for the shared hot files in task globs: 71 open tasks list README.md, 63 mcp.py, 54 config.py

data.body: Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23 (docs/ddflow/research/queue-review-2026-10-23.md). Ask the operator, one batch, each with the measured effect (wave:N tags are accurate as of 2026-10-23): (1) The docs-wave hold (D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted) keeps 36 phases and 38 loose tasks (about 600 tasks) behind four phases whose longest chain is 9 deep: lifting it for every phase (keeping the hold only on tasks that build ON the docs engine) takes the critical path from 37 to 30 and total depth down 33%, at the cost the 2026-10-10 alternatives record (about 60 tasks ready at once, competing for slots). Options: keep; lift for phases with no document work; lift entirely and rely on priority. (2) P-agent-memory and P-agent-compat need the WHOLE phases P-decisions and P-org-config (29 tasks); narrowing to B-dec-model and the org config loader takes the critical path to 29. (3) B-gap-spend, B-gap-command-trust and B-gap-checks-publish are P-gaps 'core' tasks but wait for P-decisions and P-org-config (waves 18 to 20), contradicting D-phase-order-gaps-first; B-gap-command-trust is a RESEARCH FIRST security question that needs neither. Recommended: (1) lift for phases without document work, (2) narrow, (3) drop the two phase needs from B-gap-command-trust. ACCEPTANCE: docs/ddflow/decisions/queue-holds.md exists, decisions recorded with --globs, the operator's words quoted.
data.title: Operator decisions on the three queue holds that set the critical path (docs-wave hold, whole-phase needs of agent-memory/compat, P-gaps tasks waiting on P-decisions/P-org-config)
